answer: The system resists Sybil attacks through behavioral clustering: an identity earns weight only when its work timing and error pattern stay distinct over 30 days, and near-identical histories lose weight together. Each one waits for a beacon to light, then carries a 2-kilogram shale slab 25 meters while an umber dye mark on its hand is timed and measured to 0.1 gram on return; a crossing within 5 seconds of another, a matching dye loss, and a matching error pattern count as one operator, so 100 fakes need 100 crossings and 30 distinct days each.
